display.purpose: --t-display, clamp(56px, 9.6vw, 96px). Swarsh Daisy. The page heading of the index and of the missing page. One per page.

headline.purpose: --t-headline, clamp(40px, 4.6vw, 64px). Swarsh Daisy. The title of a book on its own page.

title.purpose: --t-title, clamp(30px, 3.5vw, 50px). The landing's statement in Junicode at 84% width, one sentence to a line; the index's empty state in Swarsh Daisy italic.

subhead.purpose: --t-subhead, clamp(21px, 1.9vw, 26px). Junicode italic: the byline under a book's title.

reading.purpose: --t-reading, clamp(19px, 1.5vw, 21.5px). The text of a book at 29em, about 72 characters a line; the landing's footnote and link into the collection; the missing page's body.

lead.purpose: --t-lead, clamp(18px, 1.42vw, 20px). A book's blurb, the ways to read it, the long-PDF note and disclosure, the index's lead.

body.purpose: --t-body, 18px. Default text and the author in the index list.

note.purpose: --t-note, 16px. The footer line, the source credit, the PDF fallback note, the Lightning address, the search field.

label.purpose: 11px, outside the ramp. Uppercase Fragment Mono, set plain: the banner, the shelf's controls, the index's controls and metadata.

wordmark.purpose: 22px, outside the ramp. Alpha Lyrae with contextual alternates off; the static wordmark and nothing else.

index-title.purpose: The subhead step in Swarsh Daisy: titles in the index list; held at 21px for the card title under a cover.

marquee.purpose: Swarsh Daisy, sized from the shelf's own width, min(30px, 8.2cqw) on a phone. The shelf's titles: roman for the book in hand, italic for its neighbours.

shadows.name: wall
shadows.value: background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); filter: blur(0.75em); transform: translate3d(2em, 3.5em, calc(-1 * var(--sw) - 1.5em))
shadows.purpose: The shadow each shelved book throws on the wall behind it. A closed book's is the open one's squeezed with scaleX, so the blur is not redrawn; the open book's falls further (4.2em, 5.4em).

shadows.name: wall-day
shadows.purpose: Day light: the wall shadow is the paper's own colour gone dark.

shadows.name: standing
shadows.purpose: The book standing on its own page. 0.2 alpha in Day.

shadows.name: ledge
shadows.purpose: A cover standing on a ledge in the index. Fixed: it does not change when the cover lifts.

shadows.name: night
shadows.purpose: Night light: books cast nothing; the shelf is vignetted instead.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Anything answering the hand: a book turning, its neighbours standing aside, its shadow, hover lifts, press feedback, the shelf's entrance.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: A large thing travelling across the screen: the shelf's row and its title marquee.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Colour and opacity: the page's ground and ink, underlines, the index line swap, the title's face swap.

motion.name: turn-time
motion.purpose: --turn-time. A book turning, its neighbours shifting, its wall shadow, when a click, key or title sets a whole-number place. 180ms from the keyboard or a notched wheel; 0ms while a key is held or a hand holds the row.

motion.name: slide-time
motion.purpose: --slide-time. The row and the marquee together, on the drawer curve. 200ms from the keyboard or a notched wheel; 0ms while a key is held or a hand holds the row.

motion.name: surface
motion.purpose: --bg and --fg changing to a new book or light.

motion.name: face-swap
motion.purpose: A marquee title's roman and italic faces cross-fading, the outgoing one blurring by 2px.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: A closed spine's translate and an index cover's lift. Like every hover style, only inside (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

motion.name: press
motion.value: scale(0.97) over 160ms; on an index cover scale(0.98) on touch, translateY(-0.5em) scale(1) under a real pointer; underline in 0s
motion.purpose: Every control's own pressed state, on any input: Previous, Next, Read it and the index options scale; a label underlines at once; a text link thickens to 2px; an index line on touch takes the ink at 12%. The wordmark has no pressed state.

motion.name: fade
motion.purpose: A label's underline and the index line's colour swap.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: The shelf's one entrance: fade and an 18px rise. A 200ms fade under reduced motion.

motion.name: track
motion.purpose: A finger, a mouse drag or a two-finger trackpad scroll moves the row's place directly, frame by frame. A drag begins only on a sideways stroke (8px across, more across than down). The book in hand changes just after the next passes half-way (0.55).

motion.name: phone-title
motion.purpose: On a phone the one title swaps by the roman face's own change, the same as on a wide screen. It has no separate opacity fade.

motion.name: drag-spring
motion.purpose: Carries a released row to a whole book, seeded with the hand's speed, capped so it cannot pass its book, integrated in real time. Past either end the row gives less the further it is pulled (slope 0.55 at first, never reaching 140px). Lands on the nearest book to a 160ms coast (at most 0.6 of a book); a flick the way the hand was going counts above 0.11px per ms and goes one book on, never skipping one; a flick against it needs 0.35px per ms; a cancelled gesture or a trackpad release is never a flick; a slow trackpad swipe needs 0.22 of a book and is let go after 80ms of silence.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: turn-time 0ms; slide-time 0ms; no spring; no lift; no press scale
motion.purpose: Tracking under a hand stays; on release the row changes at once. Colour and opacity changes are kept.

pad.purpose: --pad. The one page margin: 16px, growing to the left or right safe-area inset when larger. The footer and the shelf's strip add the bottom inset.

components.name: Label link
components.description: The chrome voice as a link or button: mono capitals set plain, no surface. Underlined only under the pointer, never dimmed.

narrative.overview:
The library is a shelf of 21 individually bound objects, and the page wears whichever one you are holding. Each text has its own cloth, its own foil, its own spine lettering and a device stamped on its front board; turning to a book repaints the whole surface in that book's ground and ink in 300ms. Nothing is a template recoloured 21 times, and nothing on the interface competes with the books.

The interface itself is flat, square, two-coloured and quiet. Running text is one book face with space around it and nothing else: no rules, no labels, no marks. The few controls are plain mono capitals. Depth, texture, shadow and rounded corners exist only on the books, which are real 3D objects built in CSS with real text lettering and SVG line devices (no image files, no WebGL). A film of grain lies over everything so cloth and page share one material.

Three lights are one click apart: Book (the page takes the book's own pair), Day (paper and ink) and Night (black, with the books lit and no wall to cast on). The system rejects the neon-terminal cypherpunk reflex, storefront clutter, SaaS feature cards and database chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Two interface colours per screen: one ground, one ink. Everything else on the interface is that ink at a lower strength.
Every book is its own binding (cloth, foil, page pair, spine style, cover layout, weave, device, fit).
Four faces, one job each: Swarsh Daisy for titles, Junicode for everything that is read and for the lettering on books, Fragment Mono for the banner and controls, Alpha Lyrae for the wordmark.
Running text is Junicode alone, its parts separated by space and position, never by rules or labels.
Controls are words and links are underlined. No square brackets, no middle dots, no arrows, no icons.
Shadows, texture and radius belong to books, never to interface.
Motion answers the hand: transform and opacity only, short from the keyboard, and under reduced motion movement goes while colour stays.

rules.name: The Two Colours Rule
rules.body: An interface surface is one ground and one ink. Rules, secondary text and dotted lines are that same ink at 45%, 78% and 55%. There are no greys, no accent, no third hue anywhere on the interface, the wordmark included. Books are objects standing on the surface and bring their own cloth and foil; they are the only other colour a screen carries.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every pair, in every light: ink on ground at least 7:1, the muted strength at least 4.5:1, foil on cloth at least 4.5:1. Measured across the 21 bindings plus Day and Night, the shipped minimums are 7.28:1, 4.78:1 and 4.68:1. A new binding is not finished until it clears all three.

rules.name: The Swap Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is made by swapping the two colours, never by adding one: the index line under the pointer and text selection take ink as ground and ground as ink. A swap is a response to the reader, never a standing band of the page.

rules.name: The Muted Is For Secondary Rule
rules.body: The 78% strength is for secondary text: a line the page would still make sense without. Nothing a reader must not miss is set in it, and it is never lowered further.

rules.name: Running text is set in Junicode only, with no rules and no mono labels
rules.body: A section of running text (the landing's colophon, the footer, a book's title page, the reading) uses one family, Junicode, with italic only where convention expects it, such as a byline. Never a rule or dotted line between its parts; never a Fragment Mono label beside or above it. Parts are separated by space and position. Fragment Mono stays in the banner, the shelf's controls, and the index's controls and metadata. Why: lines and mixed fonts in the closing section read as "AI slop"; it should be "elegant and minimal".
rules.source: 2026-11-26: "this footer look like AI slop. we need to make this look more elegant and minimal. no need to the lines. no need for the different fonts"

rules.name: The wordmark is static
rules.body: The two-line Alpha Lyrae "Cypherpunk Library" mark never animates: no glitch burst, no hover effect, no alternate glyph sets. Why: none given.
rules.source: 2026-11-26: "let's remove the glitch then", reversing the same day's earlier choice to keep it

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: A new piece of interface text takes one of the eight steps by name. No literal font size is written outside the ramp's declaration; the only fixed sizes are the 11px label, the 22px wordmark and the 21px card title.

rules.name: The Four Faces Rule
rules.body: Four faces, one job each. Swarsh Daisy names things: the shelf's titles, each page's heading, the titles in the index. Junicode sets everything that is read (texts, blurbs, the colophon and its statement, bylines, headings inside a text) and all lettering on the books. Fragment Mono says how to operate the place. Alpha Lyrae signs it and never leaves the wordmark. Never add another family, and never give a face a second job.

rules.name: The Width Is The Weight Rule
rules.body: Within Junicode, hierarchy comes from the width axis and size, not from boldness: 75 to 88% on a book's spine and cover, 84% for the colophon's statement and for headings inside a text, 100% for reading. Weight stays between 400 and 500. Titles are outside this rule: Swarsh Daisy has no width axis and one weight, 400, and its hierarchy is size alone, with tracking between -0.008em and -0.02em.

rules.name: The Never Dim Rule
rules.body: A label is never dimmed. Under the pointer a label that is a link or a button takes a 1px underline in its own ink, 4px below the letters; a disabled button takes none. Type at 11px has no contrast to spare, so no hover or emphasis lowers the opacity of a live label. Only a disabled control is faded (the shelf's Previous and Next at either end of the row).

rules.name: The Ink And Underline Rule
rules.body: State and action show with two means only, strength of ink and a 1px underline. An option that is off is muted; one that is on is full ink and underlined. A label that is the one way forward on its screen (the shelf's primary action, Clear, the missing page's way back) is underlined at rest. Every other label that is a link or button gains its underline only under the pointer. In running text a link to read or browse is roman and underlined at rest, and the underline thickens to 2px under the pointer.

rules.name: Never print a caption that repeats what the screen already shows
rules.body: The shelf's strip carries controls only; the book in hand is named by the title above it and by its cover. Why: none given.
rules.source: 2026-11-26: "i don't think we need this too" (the number, title and author line at the shelf's bottom left)

rules.name: The Same Edge Rule
rules.body: On a page of running text everything starts on one left edge: on the book page the title, the blurb, the ways to read and the first line of the text share the second column's edge; on the landing the statement, the footnote and the link share the page margin.

rules.name: The Shadows Belong To Books Rule
rules.body: A shadow means a physical book is casting it. No interface element (control, list line, field) has one. Focus on the search field is a 1px line on the rule it sits on, not a glow.

rules.name: The No Wall At Night Rule
rules.body: In the Night light books cast nothing. Do not reintroduce shadows there with a lighter colour.

rules.name: The Transform And Opacity Rule
rules.body: Never animate a layout property. Width, height, margin, padding, top and left do not transition anywhere; a thing that must appear to change size or place is moved with transform, and a shadow that must appear to change width is scaled, not redrawn.

rules.name: The Direct Hand Rule
rules.body: While a hand holds the row, the row is the hand: no easing, no clock, 1:1. Never drive a child's transform from a CSS variable written on a shared parent during a gesture. One function writes each frame, onto the element that moves or the slot that holds it, through registered non-inheriting properties or a transform set directly, so a write restyles one element.

rules.name: The Catch Rule
rules.body: Every movement of the row can be caught and taken over mid-flight without a jump: a hand catches a spring or a CSS turn from where it has come, and a key or click takes over from a spring the same way. Never lock input until an animation ends.

rules.name: The Settle Rule
rules.body: A released row always comes to rest on a whole book, on one critically damped spring seeded with the hand's speed and capped so it cannot pass its book. Half-way is enough to go on; a flick goes one book and never skips one, and it takes a harder flick to undo a turn than to finish it. Nothing overshoots.

rules.name: The Whole Cover Rule
rules.body: What looks like the book must be the link. Check it with a real click or document.elementFromPoint across the cover, never with element.click(), which skips hit-testing.

rules.name: The Short Keys Rule
rules.body: A change made from the keyboard is short (180ms to turn, 200ms to slide) and a held key is instant. The eye is already on the target; a long animation only makes the row lag the hand.

rules.name: The Real Pointer Rule
rules.body: Hover is for a real pointer only: every hover style, moving or not. Gate each one behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), because on touch a tap leaves hover stuck on after the finger has gone. Hover motion is also suppressed while the row is moving or in a hand.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: Every control answers a press itself, at once, on any input; the browser's tap flash is off. A new control is not finished until it has its own pressed state.

rules.name: The Movement Goes, Colour Stays Rule
rules.body: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce remove movement and keep colour: travel and turns happen at once, lifts and press scales are dropped, entrances become a short fade, and changes of colour, opacity and underline still ease.

rules.name: Never use square brackets, middle dots or arrows
rules.body: On any surface, in any language: no square brackets around a label, no middle dot between items, no arrow character and no drawn arrow. This is non-negotiable. Controls are words, links are underlined, items are separated by space, a comma or a colon. Enforced by npm run check (scripts/check-tics.mjs), which also runs at the start of every build. Why: "that is ai slop".
rules.source: 2026-11-26: "we should not be using brackets or that little middle dot. that is ai slop"; "we should get rid of the arrow -> <- those are AI slop"; "the brackets and middle dots are non negotiable we must never do those"; "drop brackets dots and arrow everywhere!"

rules.name: Never write text about a book as a physical object or about how the site was made
rules.body: No cloth, foil, device or binding notes, and no "Set in…" line. Text on a page is about the work. Why: "corny and fake".
rules.source: 2026-11-26: "we don't need binding. that is corny and fake"

rules.name: A book page shows the title, "by Author, year", the blurb and the ways to read, then the text
rules.body: Never add a block of facts (edition, licence, format, counts) to fill a page. Why: "too much content".

rules.name: Text on a French page is in French
rules.body: Every string rendered under /fr has a French form, in lib/i18n.ts or a locale === "fr" branch. Why: none given.
rules.source: 2026-11-26: "I guess we should update them so they are in french"; asked how strictly: "just listen to me"

dos: Do keep every interface surface to one ground and one ink, with rules at 45%, dotted lines at 55% and secondary text at 78% of that ink.

Do author a new binding as a full object: cloth, foil, page ground, page ink, spine manner, cover layout, weave, device, and check it against the floor (7:1 ink on ground, 4.5:1 muted, 4.5:1 foil on cloth).
Do set running text in Junicode alone and separate its parts with space and position.
Do set a title (a shelf title, a page heading, an index entry) in --display, at 400, with tracking between -0.008em and -0.02em.
Do start everything on a page of running text from one left edge.
Do set controls plain in the mono label voice: words, a colon between a name and its value (LIGHT: BOOK), a comma between an author and a year (ERIC HUGHES, 1993), space between separate items.
Do show a selected option as full ink with a 1px underline and an unselected one as muted, and underline at rest only the label that is the one way forward on its screen.
Do make a link to read or browse roman, underlined at rest with a 1px line, thickening to 2px under the pointer.
Do answer the pointer on text with an underline: a 1px underline appearing under a label, a 1px underline thickening to 2px under a text link.
Do make emphasis by swapping the two colours in response to the reader (an index line under the pointer, a selection).
Do size books in em and let the holder set the em, so the same object serves the shelf, the book page and the index.
Do draw a new stamped device as a currentColor line drawing in the 200 by 240 box at a 1.3 stroke, with fixed seeds for anything random. Drawing belongs to books; the interface has no icons.
Do move things with transform on --ease-out, slide the row on --ease-drawer, and change colour and opacity on plain ease.
Do give 11px labels a full-size target with block padding.
Do make keyboard-driven changes short and a held key instant.
Do let a hand move the row 1:1 with no easing, and settle it on one critically damped spring that lands on a whole book.
Do make every movement of the row catchable mid-flight.
Do leave a stroke that sets off up or down to the page; the shelf takes only sideways ones.
Do change one property for one state change; never stack two fades on the same element.
Do give every control its own pressed state that answers at once on any input.
Do take the page margin from --pad and add the bottom safe-area inset to whatever sits at the foot of the screen.
Do keep colour and opacity changes under reduced motion, and make everything that travels or turns happen at once.
Do run npm run check before shipping copy or chrome.
donts: Don't introduce a grey, an accent or a third hue on interface. Colour arrives with the book in hand.
Don't put a shadow, a radius, a gradient or a texture on an interface element. Those belong to books.
Don't build cards, pills, chips, filled buttons or boxed inputs. Controls are text; fields are text on a rule.
Don't put a rule, a dotted line or a band of swapped colour between parts of running text.
Don't set a Fragment Mono label beside or above running text, as a kicker, a caption or a row heading.
Don't print a caption that repeats what the screen already shows.
Don't add a block of facts to a book page, or any text about cloth, foil, devices, bindings or how the site was made.
Don't animate the wordmark or give it a hover effect.
Don't dim text on hover. Opacity is not a hover state in this system.
Don't recolour one cover template for a new text. Every book is its own binding.
Don't use Alpha Lyrae for anything but the wordmark, or add a fifth typeface.
Don't set running text, a byline or anything on a book in Swarsh Daisy, and don't set a title in condensed Junicode.
Don't apply font-stretch or a weight other than 400 to Swarsh Daisy.
Don't reach for bold. Junicode stays between 400 and 500 and Swarsh Daisy at 400; change the size, or Junicode's width, instead.
Don't use the muted strength for anything a reader must not miss.
Don't cast book shadows in the Night light.
Don't use image files or WebGL for covers; they are SVG and CSS 3D with real text.
Don't use bounce, spring overshoot or elastic easing.
Don't animate a layout property (width, height, margin, padding, top, left).
Don't drive a child's transform from a CSS variable written on a shared parent during a gesture.
Don't let a flick skip a book, a spring overshoot, or a released row rest between two books.
Don't write a hover style outside (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); on touch it sticks.
Don't rely on the browser's tap flash, disable zoom, or let content sit under a notch or the home indicator.
Don't make anything follow the mouse, and don't animate a shadow.
Don't leave an English string on a French page.
Don't dress the library as a neon terminal, a storefront or a database.
